literal: Having strived and hoarded, 'we are destitute of support,' they will say—those who do not attain the sacrifice of hosting guests.
translation: Those who fail to perform the sacrifice of hosting guests will later lament, 'We hoarded wealth with great pain, yet we are now left with nothing.'
modern: விருந்தினர்களை உபசரித்து அந்த வேள்வியைச் செய்யாதவர்கள், 'நாங்கள் கஷ்டப்பட்டுச் சேர்த்துப் பாதுகாத்த செல்வத்தை இழந்து ஆதரவற்றவர் ஆனோம்' என்று பின்னாளில் வருந்துவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of hoarding wealth without using it for hospitality. The word 'parintu' indicates the pain and effort taken to accumulate wealth, and 'ōmpi' means guarding or hoarding it. Those who do not engage in the noble sacrifice ('vēḷvi') of hosting guests ('viruntu ōmpi') will eventually lose their wealth and lament that they have no support ('paṟṟu aṟṟēm'). The poet emphasizes that wealth not shared with guests is ultimately lost, leaving the hoarder destitute.
